subject: Issue accepting supplier invite — DNS suffix rewrites blocking portal
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@ardanttrades.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@ardanttrades.com
Date: 2026-10-21T14:12:00-04:00
Subject: Trouble accepting your supplier invite

Hi Naomi,

We received the supplier portal invite but when we click the Accept link it lands on a page that errors with "Invalid tenant binding" and then redirects to our corporate SSO (which shows a 403). This is happening for two users here (myself and our AP manager). We tried in incognito and different browsers.

I attached a short HAR/trace and our W-9 in case you need it. Can you check whether the invite was scoped to a different tenant or if there's an alias rewrite on our DNS? Our infra team said our mailflow rewrites @ardanttrades.co to @ardanttrades.com for legacy reasons — maybe that's relevant.

Thanks,
Lina Gomez
Procurement Lead
Ardant Trades

Attachments: ardant_w9.pdf (attachment stub), portal-sso-trace.txt (attachment stub)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@ardanttrades.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-21T15:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting your supplier invite

Hi Lina — thanks for the quick report and for attaching the W-9. Sorry you're running into this.

Short answers up front:
- We can see the invite was issued to lina.gomez@ardanttrades.com (the account in our system).
- If your mailflow or DNS rewrites to a different suffix we sometimes see a tenant alias mismatch on the Coupa/Zip acceptors.

Plan: I'm looping in Ben (our CS lead) and Rafael (identity engineer) to confirm what the portal is seeing and to provide a one-click alternate accept link if needed. In the meantime, can you confirm whether you or your AP manager have previously been invited under the older @ardanttrades.co address? That would help us decide if this needs a merge.

I'll keep this thread for tracking.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-10-21T16:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting your supplier invite

Adding initial troubleshooting notes and a proposed quick fix.

I pulled the invite record: token id tidy-8f3b, target_email lina.gomez@ardanttrades.com, issued 2026-10-20T18:43Z, portal: Coupa (v2). Coupa's accept flow validates the email -> tenant mapping using the inbound email domain. If Ardant's inbound rewrite maps "@ardanttrades.co" -> "@ardanttrades.com" at the MX/relay layer, the Coupa redirect may see a mismatch between token recipient and SSO assertion nameid. That yields the Invalid tenant binding you saw.

Workaround we can try right away: generate a one-time invite link bound to the tenant id rather than the email alias (token: tenant-accept-9c4). That bypasses the email nameid check and should let the two users accept. I'll generate that link and send it to Naomi to forward to Lina.

Longer term: Rafael, can you confirm whether our portal tenant mapping for Ardant includes both .co and .com aliases? If not, we should add the legacy suffix as an accepted alias to avoid recurring issues. Also we should record this under the Ardant account as "email-suffix-rewrite" for postmortem.

—Ben

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@ardanttrades.com>, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T10:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting your supplier invite

Hi Lina — Rafael here from identity engineering. Thanks for the HAR and the note about your internal rewrite. I reviewed the trace: the SAML assertion NameID is arriving as lina.gomez@ardanttrades.co while our invite token expects @ardanttrades.com. That mismatch is the exact cause of the 403.

What I did:
- Issued a tenant-bound one-time link (tenant-accept-9c4) that ignores NameID for assertion acceptance; the link expires in 24 hours.
- Added ardanttrades.co as an accepted alias on the Ardant tenant in the tenant-mapping table.

Next steps for you:
1) Please try the new link (below). If it succeeds, you'll be able to finish the supplier profile and confirm the W-9.
2) If any user still hits a 403, reply with the SSO error id (it will show on the coupa error page) and attach the portal-sso-trace.txt again.

Temporary link (one-time): https://invite.redwood.ai/tenant-accept/tenant-accept-9c4

If the link works, I'll follow up later to make the alias change permanent and update our onboarding playbook so CS engineers add the legacy suffix to new accounts when needed.

—Rafael Mendes
Identity Engineer
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
